overview: Smoore International is the world's largest ODM/OEM manufacturer of vaping and atomization devices, supplying leading global tobacco companies (notably British American Tobacco) and independent vaping brands with closed-system e-cigarette hardware, heat-not-burn (HNB) devices, and special-purpose atomization products, while also selling its own VAPORESSO-branded open-system vapes and MOYAL beauty-atomization devices. Founded by Chen Zhiping (who together with concert parties holds roughly 40% of shares) and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in July 2020, the Group reports in RMB and operates manufacturing out of Shenzhen, China, selling predominantly into Europe and the United States, with a smaller and declining mainland China contribution. It is also building out adjacent businesses in inhalation drug-device therapeutics (via U.S. subsidiary Transpire Bio) and beauty atomization.

business_model.summary: Smoore makes money primarily as a contract manufacturer (ODM/OEM) of vaping and HNB hardware for tobacco majors and independent brands (Corporate Client Oriented, 'ToB' business, ~80% of revenue), supplemented by direct sales of its own branded vaping and beauty devices (Self-Branded business, ~20% of revenue). Revenue is largely transactional/order-based (device and component sales tied to customer launch cycles and sell-through) rather than subscription-style recurring revenue, though long-term platform/technology partnerships (e.g., with BAT on HNB) create multi-year revenue visibility once a product is rolled out. Customers are overwhelmingly B2B (global tobacco companies and independent vape brands) for the ToB segment, with a B2C component via its own VAPORESSO and MOYAL retail brands.
business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2B (global tobacco majors and independent vaping brands as ODM/OEM clients) with a B2C retail component through self-branded VAPORESSO and MOYAL products
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025 revenue: Europe and other international markets ~65.9% (Self-branded 16.4% + ToB 49.5%), United States ~32.3% (Self-branded 3.7% + ToB 28.6%), Mainland China ~1.8% (Self-branded 0.3% + ToB 1.5%); manufacturing concentrated in Shenzhen, China

main_competitors: Shenzhen Vapesoul / other Shenzhen-based vape ODMs
British American Tobacco in-house/other HNB device suppliers (Philip Morris's IQOS ecosystem as a competing HNB platform)
competitive_position.market_position: World's largest vaping device manufacturer by the company's own disclosure, citing Frost & Sullivan data showing an approximately 14.5% share of the global vaping device market in 2025 (up from ~13.1% in 2024); global No.1 in open-system vaping via its VAPORESSO brand; a newly established, non-exclusive key technology supplier to BAT's glo Hilo HNB platform since 2024-2025

moat_factors.description: Decade-plus of proprietary atomization R&D (ceramic coil/heating technology under the FEELM brand), ~11,300 cumulative patent filings including over 6,000 invention patents, giving it a technical edge in flavor delivery, leak prevention and compliant device design that is difficult for smaller ODMs to replicate quickly

Scale and in-house compliance/legal infrastructure let Smoore navigate PMTA, EU flavor/battery/packaging rules and emerging bans faster than smaller or illicit competitors, turning regulatory tightening into a share-gain opportunity rather than a pure headwind
Large-scale Shenzhen manufacturing base with automation investment provides cost and quality advantages, though gross margin has been compressed by mix shift toward lower-margin products

Deep co-development relationships with major tobacco companies (e.g., BAT glo Hilo, in which Smoore provided the full R&D solution) create switching costs once a platform is jointly developed and commercialized, but tobacco majors retain multiple ODM relationships (e.g., RLX) and could dual/multi-source
VAPORESSO is the global No.1 open-system vape brand with continued share gains, but open-system is a slower-growing, more commoditized sub-segment (~3% CAGR) versus closed-system

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a small number of large tobacco-company ODM customers for the ToB segment, creating customer concentration risk
Gross margin has fallen from 53.6% (FY2021) to 34.1% (FY2025) as higher-margin legacy vaping mix has been diluted by lower-margin HNB ramp and product mix shift
No pricing power over end-retail; Smoore is a manufacturer/technology provider, not the consumer-facing brand, for ~80% of revenue
Business is exposed to the volatile and often adversarial regulatory treatment of nicotine/vaping products globally
Inhalation therapy (Transpire Bio) segment is a persistent drag on group profit (RMB132 million loss in H1 2026) while still pre-commercial

growth_drivers: HNB ramp-up: scalable shipments to a strategic customer (BAT's glo Hilo) launched in Japan, Poland and Italy in 2025, generating over RMB1.2 billion of HNB revenue in FY2025 and growing ~322% YoY to ~RMB962 million in H1 2026 alone; HNB industry seen as early-penetration with a projected ~10-11.5% unit CAGR to 2030

U.S. vaping market reopening: intensified FDA enforcement against illicit/non-compliant products (Congress appropriated $200m+ to FDA) and the May 2026 FDA authorization of the first non-tobacco/non-menthol flavored ENDS products are reviving the compliant/legal U.S. market, where Smoore's ODM customers hold an estimated 40%+ share of tracked retail channels
European closed-system vaping share gains as disposable bans (France, Belgium and others) force a shift to compliant closed-pod/rechargeable systems that favor agile, compliant ODMs like Smoore
Self-branded VAPORESSO continued momentum (record self-branded revenue in FY2025, +17.6% YoY) via product iteration (XROS series) and channel/geographic expansion

Emerging/new verticals: inhalation drug-device therapeutics (Transpire Bio - three ANDAs filed as first filer, cGMP-certified Florida facility) and beauty atomization (MOYAL) as longer-dated optionality
Industry consolidation: management expects tightening global regulation to squeeze out smaller/non-compliant competitors and concentrate share with scaled, compliant manufacturers such as Smoore

business.description: A large share of incremental growth (HNB) is tied to a single strategic customer relationship (BAT); any slowdown, renegotiation, or loss of that relationship would be highly impactful

Illegal, unauthorized vaping products (often cheaper, flavored disposables) continue to compete for share in the U.S. and elsewhere; enforcement intensity (and thus Smoore's relative advantage) can fluctuate with political and administrative priorities

business.risk: Margin erosion from product/geographic mix shift
business.description: Gross margin has nearly halved from FY2021 peak (53.6%) to FY2025 (34.1%) and fell further to 32.2% in H1 2026 as lower-margin HNB and special-purpose products grow faster than legacy vaping
Inhalation therapy (Transpire) remains loss-making and pre-commercial; beauty atomization is a nascent, unproven consumer category

financial.risk: Declining cash balances and rising debt
financial.description: Cash and equivalents fell from RMB7.3bn (FY2025) to RMB4.0bn (H1 2026); total debt has risen from near-zero in FY2022 to RMB335m-1,875m across recent periods, alongside a US$80 million zero-coupon note subscription in October 2025
Revenue is substantially USD/EUR-denominated while costs and reporting are RMB-based; FY2025 recorded a net FX loss of RMB150.9 million versus a gain the prior year

financial.risk: Rising share-based compensation and compliance costs
financial.description: SBC expense jumped to RMB468m in FY2025 (from RMB206m in FY2024) and legal/compliance professional fees rose ~139% YoY, both compressing reported profit even as adjusted profit held up better

regulatory.description: FDA has issued marketing denial orders against the vast majority of non-tobacco/non-menthol flavored ENDS submissions; litigation over MDOs continues through federal appellate courts and the Supreme Court; policy can swing between strict enforcement and more permissive guidance (as seen with the May 2026 authorization of flavored products), creating ongoing uncertainty for customer product lines manufactured by Smoore

regulatory.risk: EU/UK flavor, disposable and battery bans
regulatory.description: Growing list of EU states banning disposable vapes or restricting flavors (10+ countries with flavor restrictions as of Dec 2025, more considering it); UK's Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) Regulations took effect June 2025 and a broader Tobacco and Vapes Bill is progressing through Parliament; each regulatory change forces costly product redesign but can also favor compliant large manufacturers over smaller players

Hong Kong enacted the Tobacco Control Legislation (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 banning possession of alternative smoking products; mainland China's State Council issued December 2025 opinions on cracking down on illegal e-cigarette production and 'addictive' e-cigarettes, tightening customs/tobacco-authority supervision

regulatory.risk: U.S. rescheduling of special-purpose atomization products
regulatory.description: Management flags a potential benefit from anticipated U.S. rescheduling of certain special-purpose atomization products to a less-controlled category in 2026, but the outcome and timing are uncertain and could also go the other way

macro.description: Vaping/nicotine products exhibit relatively inelastic demand versus typical consumer discretionary goods, but self-branded and beauty-atomization segments carry some cyclicality

H1 2026 results cited adverse logistics impact from Middle East geopolitical tensions on self-branded vaping shipments; broader US-China trade tension is a latent risk given Shenzhen-based manufacturing serving US/EU end markets
Cost of raw materials rose from 47.7% to 50.5% of revenue in FY2025, partly mix-driven; batteries, electronic components and e-liquid/flavor compounds are the primary inputs

execution.risk: Reliance on single strategic HNB customer ramp
execution.description: The HNB growth story depends heavily on BAT's glo Hilo multi-market rollout executing well commercially; any stumble in BAT's own go-to-market would directly hit Smoore's fastest-growing segment

Management is 'proactively advancing external equity financing' for Transpire to offload its cash/profit drag and unlock value; execution of any such financing or eventual spin-out/partnership is not yet finalized

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global vaping device market (ex-factory price) grew at an ~8.9% CAGR 2021-2025 and is projected to grow ~9.1% CAGR 2025-2030 per Frost & Sullivan; closed-system vaping (Smoore's core ODM category) is forecast to grow faster (~10.6% CAGR 2025-2030) than open-system (~3.4%); global HNB stick volumes are projected to grow from ~204 billion units (2025) to ~352 billion units (2030), an ~11.5% CAGR, as tobacco majors position HNB as a core harm-reduction growth pillar
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately low cyclicality given inelastic nicotine demand, but revenue growth is highly sensitive to regulatory cycles (bans, enforcement waves, PMTA rulings) rather than the broader economic cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate; the company holds net cash historically (though declining) and modest debt (including a new US$80m zero-coupon note), so higher rates have a mild net negative effect via lower interest income on cash balances and raise the cost of any future debt issuance
key_input_costs: E-liquid/flavor compounds and raw materials for atomization devices

recent_developments.event: Interim results: revenue up 19.9% YoY to RMB7,209 million (record H1), but gross margin fell to 32.2% from 37.3% on product mix; HNB revenue surged ~322% YoY to ~RMB962 million; profit for the period up 16.2% to RMB572 million while total comprehensive income fell 46.1% largely on FX/other comprehensive items

FDA authorized the first non-tobacco, non-menthol flavored ENDS products (mango- and blueberry-flavored, with Bluetooth device-access restriction) and issued new enforcement-priority guidance de-prioritizing products with pending, accepted/filed premarket applications — a meaningful shift toward a more permissive compliant-product environment in the U.S.

FDA issued draft guidance proposing a higher evidentiary bar for sweet/dessert-flavored ENDS products lacking device-access restriction features, continuing to shape compliant product design requirements

BAT's glo Hilo HNB product (co-developed with Smoore) launched nationwide in Japan, the largest HNB market by volume, with rollout also underway in Poland and Italy; FY2025 HNB revenue exceeded RMB1.2 billion, Smoore's first scalable HNB shipments after a decade of R&D investment
Hong Kong's Legislative Council passed the Tobacco Control Legislation (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, tightening restrictions on alternative smoking products
Smoore subscribed to US$80 million of callable zero-coupon notes, adding to balance-sheet debt

Full-year results: record revenue of RMB14,256 million (+20.8% YoY) but profit fell 18.5% YoY to RMB1,062 million on higher share-based compensation and legal/compliance costs; adjusted profit (ex-SBC) rose 1.3% to RMB1,530 million; Board proposed a final dividend of HK20 cents per share
China's State Council issued 'Opinions on Whole-Chain Crackdown of Tobacco-Related Illegal Activities,' tightening e-cigarette supervision and customs/tobacco-authority data sharing in mainland China

UBS downgraded Smoore from Neutral to Sell, citing valuation concerns and a conservative view of earnings potential from BAT's HNB ramp (target price HK$10.72), while CICC maintained Outperform with a HK$23 target the following month, raising its FY2026 net profit forecast ~11% on expected large-scale HNB stick shipments

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / FY2025 Annual Report (Chairman's Statement and Outlook)

items.target: Expand premium HNB product rollout with the strategic customer (BAT) to more markets globally beyond the initial nine launched markets
items.notes: Qualitative commitment, no numeric revenue target disclosed; HNB described as the 'second horizon' growth driver

items.target: Expect to 'unlock growth opportunities' and help customers 'regain market share' following May 2026 FDA enforcement-priority shift
items.vs_prior: raised (more optimistic tone vs prior periods)
items.notes: Qualitative; tied to FDA's new enforcement posture and key customers' planned new product launches

items.target: Potential benefit from anticipated U.S. rescheduling of relevant products to a less-controlled category, supporting 'healthy and compliant market growth'
items.notes: Contingent on a regulatory rescheduling decision that has not yet occurred as of the reports reviewed

items.target: Continue 'enhanced R&D efficiency' and accelerate commercialization; prioritize HNB and inhalation therapy platforms
items.notes: FY2025 R&D fell 3.1% YoY to RMB1,523m (10.7% of revenue, down from 13.3%) due to efficiency gains and capitalization of qualifying development costs; H1 2026 R&D rose 16.9% YoY to RMB845m on higher HNB investment

items.target: Continue to 'advance the external equity financing of Transpire' to unlock its value and mitigate its drag on Group profit and cash flow
items.notes: No specific terms, timeline or valuation disclosed; Transpire posted a RMB132m loss in H1 2026

items.target: Final dividend of HK20 cents per ordinary share proposed for FY2025
items.vs_prior: n/a - first disclosed in FY2025 annual report reviewed
items.notes: No explicit payout-ratio policy or FY2026 dividend guidance disclosed in the materials reviewed

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Chen Zhiping frames 2025 as a 'pivotal year' with HNB as the Group's 'second horizon' delivering its first scalable shipments, alongside continued vaping growth from tighter global enforcement against non-compliant products. For 2026, management expects to 'achieve its planned milestones,' emphasizing disciplined execution, deepening the BAT HNB partnership into more markets, capitalizing on the more favorable May 2026 U.S. FDA enforcement stance to help ODM customers regain U.S. share, and continuing cost/compliance discipline, while flagging legal/compliance costs and share-based compensation as near-term margin pressures.

bull_case: HNB is a multi-decade, high-growth secular category (global sticks volume CAGR ~11.5% through 2030) where Smoore is the key enabling technology/manufacturing partner to a major tobacco company (BAT), giving it a credible path to a large new profit pool beyond its mature vaping ODM base

Tightening global regulation (EU disposable bans, intensified US FDA enforcement against illicit products) is structurally favoring large, compliant, well-capitalized manufacturers like Smoore over smaller/illicit competitors, potentially accelerating industry consolidation in its favor
World's largest vaping device manufacturer with rising market share (14.5% in 2025, up from 13.1%), deep IP moat (~11,300 patents) and global No.1 open-system brand (VAPORESSO) still gaining share

May 2026 FDA shift toward authorizing flavored products and de-prioritizing enforcement against pending applicants could reopen meaningful US growth for Smoore's ODM customers after years of suppressed compliant-market volumes

Valuation has already de-rated sharply (analyst targets range from ~HK$7.6 to ~HK$23, with the stock trading well below 52-week highs), offering potential upside if HNB execution and US recovery materialize as management expects
bear_case: Profitability has deteriorated structurally: gross margin nearly halved from 53.6% (FY2021) to 34.1% (FY2025) and fell further in H1 2026 (32.2%), while reported net profit has declined for four consecutive years (FY2021-FY2025) despite revenue growth, driven by unfavorable mix shift and rising SBC/compliance costs

Heavy dependence on a single strategic HNB customer relationship (BAT) and a concentrated ODM customer base in a highly politically contested industry, where regulatory sentiment can reverse quickly (illustrated by the whiplash between FDA MDOs, court reversals, and the May 2026 authorization)

Core electronic-vaping growth is substantially attributable to the illicit market being suppressed by enforcement rather than organic underlying demand growth, meaning any softening of enforcement (as has happened before) could stall the recovery narrative

New growth bets (inhalation therapy via Transpire Bio, beauty atomization) are unproven, capital-consuming and loss-making, diluting near-term returns while management seeks external financing to offload the drag

Highly divergent analyst views (UBS Sell at HK$10.72 vs CICC Outperform at HK$23) reflect genuine uncertainty about valuation and earnings durability; declining cash balance (down ~46% H1 2026) and rising debt (including a new US$80m note) reduce the balance-sheet cushion that previously supported the bull case
